title: Again the Lord of Life and Light
description: Again the Lord of Life and Light in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anna Laetitia Barbauld wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 60 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Lord's Day Morning”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-gain the Lord of life and light A-wakes the kin-dling ray, Un-seals the eye-lids of the morn, And pours in-creas-ing day.

lines: Again the Lord of life and light
Unseals the eyelids of the morn,
O what a night was that which wrapped
O what a sun which broke, this day,
This day be grateful homage paid,
Let gladness dwell in every heart,
Ten thousand differing lips shall join
Which scatters blessings from its wings

licence: Public domain: Anna Laetitia Barbauld died in 1825.
credits: Words by Anna Laetitia Barbauld (1743–1825), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
